context_notes: This session ran 14 retroactive secure-phase audits plus one nyquist pass, covering 375 threats. The work was worth doing because it found five DISTINCT failure shapes, none of which a passing test suite would ever catch — every one is a case where the RECORD and the CODE disagreed. In rough order of value: (1) a control the register asserted that had never existed on the paths it named (50, fixed); (2) an acceptance whose premise a later plan in the same phase destroyed (59, re-accepted); (3) the declared mitigation not being the code that actually ran (47, open); (4) new attack surface added after the register was authored and never registered (51); (5) a mitigation citing an artifact never built because a checkpoint took its DROP branch (63, 58, 61 — three occurrences, so this is a register characteristic, not a one-off). The method that made these visible: tell each auditor to verify against the implementation rather than the plan's own claim, name the specific shapes already found, and forbid self-authoring a corrected rationale. Carry that forward. Suites at pause: pytest 3982 passed / 154 skipped / 0 failed; node 862 pass / 0 fail. Nothing is armed; the first live unattended credit-spending batch still has NOT run.
